judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic claim is exact. verify.json id 6 really is compare('10*8 + 1' vs '10*1 + 8') -> '>' (81 versus 18) and the study guide's id 6 compares 61 with 16, so 'including 61 versus 16 and 81 versus 18' is faithful; all six worksheet values (15, 13, 17, '<', 16, '>') and all four declared traps (51, 31, 71, 61) recompute correctly, and the ten-frame drawings match their stems. Two things the 32/32 does not survive. First, instruction_following: the prompt says 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review', and five of six items ask for one — problem 2 'Circle the digit that is in the wrong place', problem 3 'Tell why 71 is too big', problem 4 'Draw both', problem 5 'Find Ana's mistake', problem 6 'say which digit sits in the tens place'. verify.json declares zero manual entries, gate_log.txt reports '6 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual', and final_response.md states 'Nothing is flagged manual.' Second, problem 6 prints two response requirements and verify.json id 6 covers only the relation; the tens-place digit (8) appears solely as unboxed prose in the key's Step 3 — the same shape as the curr-032 finding the brief cites. The Quick Answers bank additionally prints '4. -' and '6. -' for the two compare items.

strengths_to_preserve: All four misconception traps are declared with an expr and machine-checked, not hand-typed: 51 from '10*5 + 1', 31 from '10*3 + 1', 71 from '10*7 + 1', 61 from '10*6 + 1'. The verifier proves each planted number really is what the swapped method computes and that it is distinguishable from the truth, and the key prints all four in a 'Common wrong answers' block.

The answer key's grading note is the pedagogically right frame and is worth keeping verbatim: 'A swapped answer is not a counting mistake — the child counted correctly and then wrote the digits in the wrong order', so the conversation is about place value rather than counting.

Problem 6 escalates the compare beyond a second 1-ten pair: 81 versus 18 makes the 'more tens always wins' rule do real work, and the study guide's Skill 3 try-it (61 versus 16) is a different pair from either worksheet item.
The watch-out box names the cause of the misconception rather than the symptom: teen numbers are said ones-first ('six-teen') but written tens-first, which is exactly why the digits get swapped.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md contains two rules that collide on error-analysis items, and the generator resolved the collision in the direction that produces zero manual flags. Line 249 says to reframe error-analysis 'find and fix the mistake' through the ordinary machine types; line 257 says to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. A hybrid item — explain the error AND write the corrected number — satisfies both descriptions, and nothing tells the author to split it into a machine entry for the number plus a manual entry for the explanation. The result is a misconception-analysis worksheet whose diagnosis, circling and drawing requirements are all recorded as machine-verified.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 3: 'Tell why 71 is too big, then write seventeen the correct way.' verify.json id 3 is a single eval -> 17, with no manual entry.
worksheet.tex problem 5: 'Find Ana's mistake, then write the number the dots really show.' verify.json id 5 is a single eval -> 16.
worksheet.tex problem 2 asks the student to circle a digit and problem 4 says 'Draw both'; both are recorded as machine-verified with no manual companion.
gate_log.txt step 5: '6 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual'; the run's machine observation records gate_chain_manual_flags false; final_response.md says 'Nothing is flagged manual.'
SKILL.md line 249 versus line 257 — the two rules give opposite answers for this item shape.

root_causes.description: Problem 6 prints two response requirements in one stem and the JSON covers one. Nothing in the gate chain compares printed response slots against verify entries for the same id, so a partially verified problem passes every gate.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 6: 'Write $>$ or $<$ in the blank, then say which digit sits in the tens place of Jo's swapped number' — an \ansblank plus a second asked-for value.
verify.json id 6: one compare entry, expected '>'. The digit 8 has no entry.
answer_key.tex problem 6 boxes only \ans{>}; 'The digit sitting in the tens place of Jo's swapped number is the 8' is unboxed prose, so even the answer-key binding gate never sees it.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py resolves a string 'expected' by sympify+latex and falls back to a TeX em-dash when sympify raises. A bare relation symbol is not a sympifiable expression, so every compare problem whose order is 'relation' is silently banked as '---' — the marker the module documents as 'manual-only / see solution'. The verified answer exists and is correct; the grader's quick-reference column simply refuses to print it.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '1. 15  2. 13  3. 17  4. -  5. 16  6. -' — the two em-dashes are exactly the two compare items.
verify.json ids 4 and 6 carry "order": "relation" with expected '<' and '>'; gate_log.txt records both as PASS.

improvements.title: Explain / diagnose / circle / draw sub-answers must be recorded as manual
improvements.proposed_change: Resolve the SKILL.md collision explicitly. Rewrite line 249 to say that an error-analysis item is reframed through the ordinary types ONLY for the part that produces a number; if the same item also asks the student to explain, name the error, circle, mark or draw, that part gets its own additional entry of "type": "manual" under the SAME id, with a desc stating what a grader should look for. Add the rule to references/problem-library.md's reframing section and give the generator a trigger list — 'explain', 'tell why', 'find the mistake', 'circle', 'draw', 'say which', 'is X right' — so the decision is not left to judgement. For this case, ids 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 each gain a manual companion entry and the run correctly exits 2.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_curriculum_eval_suite.py that scans a misconception-analysis task's worksheet.tex for the trigger verbs and asserts that every \problem block containing one has at least one "type": "manual" entry under its id in the paired verify.json. Run it against curr-034's retained artifacts: it must fail today (five blocks match a trigger, zero manual entries exist) and pass once the companion entries are added.
improvements.expected_impact: The 36-case systemic finding stops recurring. Concretely, a misconception-analysis sheet stops claiming SymPy-grade verification for a child's written diagnosis, the build exits 2 with visible manual flags, and the prompt's explicit 'clearly label any genuinely open response' instruction is honoured instead of contradicted by final_response.md.
improvements.risk: Verb triggers will over-fire on stems that use 'explain' only as scaffolding in a work space (curr-084 does this correctly, routing the explanation to the work space and the checkable value to the answer line). Scope the trigger scan to the sentence containing the answer request, and keep the gate at exit 2 so an over-flag costs a reviewer's glance, not a failed build.

improvements.title: Problem 6's tens-place digit is a printed answer with no verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Split problem 6 into two entries under id 6 — the existing compare for the relation, plus an entry whose expected is the tens-place digit 8 that the stem asks the student to name — and box that value with \ans{} in the key so the answer-key binding gate can see it. Systemically, add the printed-slot-versus-verify-entry count to tests/check_layout.py described under this same issue_key in the curr-023 review, and extend it to count asked-for values in the stem prose ('then say which', 'then write both'), not only \ansblank macros.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem stem reads 'Write $>$ or $<$ in the blank, then say which digit sits in the tens place' with one \ansblank, paired with a verify JSON holding a single compare entry for that id: the checker must exit 2 naming the problem. Adding a second entry under the same id must make it exit 0. Today the single-entry fixture exits 0.
improvements.expected_impact: The second half of problem 6 — the 'which digit sits in the tens place' question that distinguishes real place-value understanding from a lucky symbol — becomes a checked, boxed answer instead of unverified prose.
improvements.risk: Same heuristic risk as the curr-023 entry: prose-phrase detection will over-fire on rhetorical questions. Keep the gate at exit 2.

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified relation symbol
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation strings in _fmt() BEFORE the sympify attempt: map '<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=' (and the unicode forms) to '$<$', '$>$', '$=$', '$\le$', '$\ge$', '$\ne$'. sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError, so today every compare entry with "order": "relation" drops into the '---' fallback that exists for genuinely unrenderable values. Keep '---' for manual-only ids and for real sympify failures, so the fallback still means 'see the worked solution'.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON of [{'id':1,'type':'compare','values':['3','7'],'order':'relation','expected':'<'}, {'id':2,'type':'compare','values':['9','4'],'order':'relation','expected':'>'}, {'id':3,'type':'manual','desc':'open'}] and asserts the bank lines are '$<$', '$>$' and '---' respectively. Today entries 1 and 2 both render '---', so the assertion fails; after the relation mapping it passes, and the manual id still prints '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores the two comparison answers ('<' for problem 4, '>' for problem 6) to the grading column of a sheet where compare is one of the two declared verification targets.
improvements.risk: Low. Bank entries stay plain text (no \ans/\boxed), so check_answer_key.py's strict per-problem boxed-answer binding is untouched, and column_count() only sees a 3-char string. The only judgement call is math-mode wrapping of '='; both '=' and '$=$' set correctly inside the multicols block.

case_summary: Six well-aimed teen-number problems whose mathematics, ten-frame drawings and four machine-derived traps (51, 31, 71, 61) are all correct, and whose answer key reframes a swapped digit as place value rather than counting. The problem is what the verification claims. Five of six items ask the child to circle, draw, explain or name an error, and the run records zero manual items while final_response.md asserts 'Nothing is flagged manual' — directly against the prompt's instruction to label open responses. Problem 6 additionally asks for two answers and verifies one, leaving the tens-place digit as unboxed prose. The Quick Answers bank also drops both compare items to em-dashes.
